outcome: Clinical outcome of missing IUD strings
cohort: 726 women who underwent post-placental or intra-cesarean IUD insertion between January 2010 and December 2012 in Balangir, Odisha, India, and had follow-up data
finding: Missing IUD strings were a common complication (209/690, 30.3%), but most cases were asymptomatic and managed conservatively, with spontaneous string descent in many cases.
mod_finding: Post-placental and intra-cesarean IUD insertion was found to be a safe and effective method of contraception, although missing strings emerged as a potential issue.
